## License
Licence text found in the repository `LICENSE` file, first heading: **"ODC Open Database License (ODbL)"**. The repository README itself states no separate licence. ODbL obligations (attribution, share-alike, keep open) should be checked by the team before redistributing derived data.

## Provenance and reliability (D3)
The README of the source repository says the data come from the **Namma BMTC 2.0 app**, which "has inaccurate data, and is known to have incorrect timetables and stop timings", and that only routes available in that app are included. It also states: "Only arrival times are published, so GTFS arrival and departure times are equal at each stop. Arrival times missing from the source are interpolated by the distance between stops." Treat this as a scraped, approximate timetable, not an official schedule.

## Quality profile (measured)
- stop_times rows: **2,238,693** across 69,642 trips and 9,936 distinct stops.
- Arrival equals departure on 100.00% of rows, so dwell time is always 0 and cannot be analysed.
- Blank arrival or departure times: 0. Duplicate (trip_id, stop_sequence): 0. Orphan trips/routes/stops: 0 / 0 / 0.
- Rows with an hour of 24 or more (after-midnight times): 2,517. They are kept by the custom time parser.
- `timepoint = 0` rows: 7,806 (0.35%).
- Calendar: 61 service_ids; 4 run on every weekday and are used for the `weekday` analysis (services running on all of Mon to Fri).

## Interpolation profile (D5)
Timetables look smooth because of how they were built. Among the 1,935,039 valid hops:
- 47.08% have a speed within 1% of their own trip's median speed; 78.85% within 5%; 93.79% within 20%.
- Mean hop speed is 20.79 km/h (std 2.37); speed percentiles p05/p25/p50/p75/p95 = [16.4, 20.85, 21.57, 21.72, 21.99] km/h.
- Using the feed's own `shape_dist_traveled`, the hop speed percentiles p05/p25/p50/p75/p95 are [21.33, 21.69, 21.88, 22.23, 27.84] km/h (1,932,622 hops compared).
- Straight-line (haversine) distance divided by `shape_dist_traveled` has p10/p50/p90 = [0.774, 0.977, 0.999], i.e. straight-line distance is usually slightly shorter than the shape distance, as expected.

**Reading:** the scheduled times are close to constant-speed between stops. Differences between hours or trips are therefore mostly rounding and route geometry, not planned congestion. This limits what any "scheduled slowdown" analysis can show (see RESULTS.md).

## Feeder / trunk classification (T13, heuristic)
- Route-name prefixes found in `route_short_name` (top): `MF-` (129), `V-` (85), `G-` (51), `KBS-` (41), `BC-` (27), `KIA-` (23), `NICE-` (22), `CHAKRA-` (22), `HAEA-` (21), `HSS-` (20), `SBS-` (19).
- `MF-` is a clear prefix (129 routes, e.g. MF-10, MF-10 D24G-KDG, MF-10A, MF-10B). The team should confirm with BMTC that `MF` means metro feeder; the code assumes it.
- Rule used: **feeder** = name starts with `MF-`; **trunk** = not feeder and median trip length at least 30 km (straight-line); **other** = the rest. This is a heuristic, not an official label.
- Count per class (routes with weekday trips):

| route_class | n_routes | mean_route_km | median_route_km |
|---|---|---|---|
| other | 3176 | 16.1 | 15.7 |
| trunk | 1009 | 37.9 | 35.8 |
| feeder | 123 | 12.0 | 11.3 |

## Responsible use (D7)
The columns present (ids, names, times, coordinates of bus stops, fares, flags) contain no personal data about riders or staff. The `feed_contact_email` field in `feed_info.txt` is the dataset maintainer's public contact, not used here.
